brief: An order card stays onscreen when a refresh swaps its handlers. The title groups the card, but people need both Open and Refund independently.
The Find rotor in a notes editor has a hit after a family emoji. The user edits an earlier paragraph before following that hit.
A coupon row has a custom typeface, a long translated description and a working Redeem button. It is configured twice at accessibility sizes.
A file is locked while an older Delete shortcut is still held. Open must remain available and unlocking should restore Delete.
A second payment sheet opens synchronously when the first restores focus. The background was already hidden by another overlay.
The editor switches to read-only while the grouped editing commands are visible. Ordinary Copy remains available.
Search highlights part of an accented character; the reader asks for the previous complete match rather than the next one.
An address form's old response arrives after an edit. Announcing validation completion can synchronously submit the updated address.
The Now Playing inspector opens while someone switches from forced translations to full captions in the system menu.
A reader switches Reduce Motion while the selected article moves to another section. The app should still show the same article.
Two lectures both have a track named English. A menu from the first stays alive as the second starts playing.
A preference is edited in Settings and echoed back by the local store. A later change by the user must still save once.
A wrapped native button is configured with a new target while disabled. It becomes enabled again before an old callback arrives.
A filtered subtitle menu does not contain the current track. A restored preference then requests a deleted option.
An animated episode card becomes static under Reduce Motion. Play and the supplementary play-from-start command must still do different things.
A font preview lets someone choose a size without changing their device. Other labels still follow the live size setting.
A filter sheet starts closing and a different filter opens. The first sheet's close request and its eventual completion arrive separately.
Two documents share an inspector class. A previously focused editor moves between windows and the fallback may refuse first responder.
A sidebar refresh removes one folder and contains the same ID in two new branches. A client still holds the old folder object.
A library outline row exposes selection and expansion and contains a separate Open button. Some rows also have Reveal in Finder.
A detachable inspector adds a keyboard loop. A plug-in updates the neighboring link before the inspector closes.
A timetable merges several slots into one appointment. Removing the appointment should clear all covered coordinates.
A reused toolbar group changes Save's keyboard help and callback. The next group has no help string.
A library inspector finds several Spanish audio choices, only one described. The listener already chose another language.
A results filter moves selection while a warning indicator still applies to the previous row. It must lose selection but keep the warning semantics.
A SwiftUI wrapper hosts an editable native search field and a Clear button. Rebuilding the surrounding view updates Clear's target.
A text field changes through dictation while validation runs. Its inline instructions must belong to the current text.
A caption options panel starts a retry. Its previous task reports cancellation after the retry succeeds.
A Mac player reloads track choices without changing movies. The external choice is still active but no longer on the list.
A detail sheet closes after its originating row is filtered out. Another document has a row with the same title.
A sidebar is reordered by date while a keyboard user is on a pinned item. The same view then removes the pinned item.
An editor's query changes and a later document edit moves the results. Earlier search shortcuts can still be invoked.
A design inspector switches between two appearances and imports swatches in different color spaces. Equivalent swatches should grade consistently.
The inspector stays open when a document temporarily has no video. Its old results must not imply the new clip has no audio.
A TV detail screen stops observing during navigation. The user changes a preference after it restarts but before an old queued closure runs.
A sports shelf reuses two buttons for a different match. The visible captions and the shortcut names must agree with the actions actually dispatched.
The selected show remains on the shelf after reordering. A removed button is reparented in a temporary stack and receives a late press.
A remote-focused download changes from a priority transfer with help to a regular transfer with no help; the file ID stays the same.
Pinning a channel updates a visible word and a selected trait. The server sometimes repeats the same pin value.
The native playback overlay is already working. A request for described audio has no eligible match on the current item.
A show-card theme accepts only opaque palettes. A designer submits a translucent mid-gray highlight.
The TV picker offers subtitle choices; one asset permits Off and another does not. A user changes between them without leaving the player.
A retry reloads the caption list for the same movie. The older request then completes and its old menu is dismissed.
A German title wraps over the Play and Details controls. Both remote actions should stay reachable and retain different destinations.
An on-screen playback-speed list belongs to a previous episode. The next episode offers a different set of rates.
A details card displays track availability. The player switches clips while metadata is still loading and preserves the audience's audio choice.
A transcript search has overlapping matches. A user who does not use the rotor still needs ordinary previous and next controls.
A wrapped UIKit button on the TV sidebar is disabled after focus moves. A replacement button has a new enabled handler.
A purchase confirmation closes and immediately reopens for the next episode. A delayed completion and then a duplicate completion arrive.
A service offers only full captions in its picker, but the player initially has a forced-only track selected.
